subject: Renewal addendum: geographic reserved pools (EU + APAC) and throughput SLAs
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Antonio Garcia <antonio.garcia@fastfin.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 5 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal addendum: proposal to add EU and APAC reserved pools + SLOs

Hi Antonio —

Thanks again for the continued partnership. As we approach your Nov 30 renewal, I wanted to surface a compact proposal so your team can review before we send the formal amendment. Key asks from FastFin last week were: 1) reduce cross-region latency for EU/APAC requests, 2) guaranteed throughput for peak trading windows, and 3) a straightforward failover behavior.

Proposed summary (attached: 2025-11-05_Redwood_FastFin_renewal_proposal_v2.pdf):
- Add two new reserved pools: EU (4-node pool, each node = 8x A100-equivalent GPUs) and APAC (3-node pool) for the 12-month renewal term.
- Commit to throughput guardrails: baseline pooled concurrency (per-region) mapped to a minimum tokens-per-second rate; we recommend reserving capacity to guarantee sustained throughput of ~1.2M tokens/min across EU pool and ~900k tokens/min across APAC during peak windows.
- Latency SLO: p95 generation latency < 350ms for prompt lengths <= 256 tokens when routed to local region and within committed throughput.
- Failover policy: automatic routing to the secondary region (EU <-> US for EU; APAC -> US for APAC) with warm KV cache priming for recent session prefixes during the 5-minute window after failover.

Can you confirm whether the EU/APAC sizes above align with your forecasting? If helpful, I can loop Neha from CS to propose a verification run and a short failover test window during the first month post-rollout.

Next steps:
- If high level looks good, I'll kick off a redlineable term-sheet (attached) and schedule a short tech sync with Karthik.

Best,
Soojin

Thanks, Soojin. High level this aligns with what we discussed. A couple of clarifying questions before we move to a contract redline: 

1) The tokens/min numbers — can you translate those to expected concurrent requests and per-request latency at 256 tokens? Our trading UI issues are sensitive to p99 tail. We need a concrete mapping so our SREs can sign off.
2) For failover: what's the expected cold-cache penalty if we failover outside the warm-priming window? We want to understand user-visible latency spikes.

Also, procurement asked for an itemized delta to the current spend and an explicit list of machines (GPU counts) so they can justify the budget to finance.

If you can send a short technical note for SRE and a redline-ready term sheet we can aim to get procurement approval within two weeks.

Antonio — quick technical note to map the numbers into something SREs can consume. TL;DR: the proposal maps to expected concurrency and worst-case cold-cache penalties below.

- GPU sizing: EU pool (4 nodes x 8 GPUs = 32 GPUs total), APAC pool (3 nodes x 8 GPUs = 24 GPUs total). Node sizes are 8x A100-equivalent; we tune quantization/instance sizes per model.
- Baseline routing and concurrency mapping: we allocate token slots per GPU based on model size and typical request length. For your current model and 256-token average responses, 1 GPU sustains ~40 concurrent short-turn (prompt+256-token) inference streams at p95 < 300ms under no other contention. So EU pool (32 GPUs) yields ~1.2k concurrent streams aggregate; APAC (24 GPUs) ~900 concurrent streams — this maps to the tokens/min figures Soojin used.
- Cold-cache penalty: if failover happens and the session KV cache is empty, p95 can spike 2x–4x for the first 10–30 seconds for long-running sessions as caches warm; however, we can mitigate with warm-priming (we will keep recent prefixes in a small persistent cache for 5 minutes).
- Autoscaling: Dedicated pools support controlled burst to shared capacity if you opt-in; that adds variable cost and cannot be part of a hard SLO. We can include a fallback SLA for availability but not for absolute guaranteed latency when bursting to shared resources.

Actionable ask: confirm target SLO percentile (we recommend p95 for contractual SLO, and p99 as an internal target to monitor). If you need p99 contractual guarantees, we need to size additional headroom (approximately +20% GPUs).

I can produce a one-page SRE note with explicit concurrency vs latency tables and sample load profiles if that helps procurement sign-off.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
